title: In an office
topic: Someone has dropped a cup at work. The cup belongs to the person on the right. Look at the picture. What does the person indicated by the arrow say?
levelRationale: N5-oriented expression matching, not English-translation recognition. Numbered choices differ in communicative purpose; tips explain less familiar scene vocabulary. Stock voices and exact output still require listening approval.

turns.speaker: n
turns.text: 絵を見て、話を聞いてください。矢印の人は、何と言いますか。答えを一つ選んでください。
turns.translation: Look at the picture and listen. What does the person indicated by the arrow say? Choose one answer.

turns.speaker: n
turns.text: 会社で、コップを落としてしまいました。コップは右の人の物です。絵を見てください。矢印の人は、何と言いますか。
turns.translation: Someone has dropped a cup at work. The cup belongs to the person on the right. Look at the picture. What does the person indicated by the arrow say?

turns.speaker: a
turns.spokenText: いち。大切に使ってください。

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: 2。貸してくれて、ありがとうございます。
turns.spokenText: に。貸してくれて、ありがとうございます。
turns.translation: 2. Thank you for lending it to me.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: 3。コップを割ってしまって、すみません。
turns.spokenText: さん。コップを割ってしまって、すみません。
turns.translation: 3. I'm sorry I broke the cup.

options.label: 大切に使ってください。
options.rationale: This tells the listener to take care of something rather than apologizing for the speaker's damage.

options.label: 貸してくれて、ありがとうございます。
options.translation: Thank you for lending it to me.
options.rationale: Thanks for a loan does not acknowledge or apologize for the stated breakage.

options.label: コップを割ってしまって、すみません。
options.translation: I'm sorry I broke the cup.
options.rationale: This acknowledges the accidental damage and apologizes to its owner.

explanation: The completed accident requires an apology from the person who caused it, not an instruction to the owner or thanks alone.

visual.description: Two coworkers stand on opposite sides of an office desk. A broken cup with a few separated pieces is on the floor by person A on the left, who still holds its detached handle. A single arrow points to A. Person B stands on the right. No speech bubbles or option labels.
